_source: Ours. The book prints every rent and every Lifestyle (Core p.377-378, in creation-rules.json) and never says what moving costs, how long it takes, or which buildings rent which kind of home. A table does not need telling; an engine does.

_rules.deposit: Moving in costs the new place's rent for depositMonths months, up front, and the landlord keeps it. Somewhere that charges no rent asks for no deposit.
_rules.time: A move takes moveMinutes on the clock: packing, hauling and the walk round with the super. Changing what you eat moves nothing and takes no time.
_rules.bills: Nobody moves out owing. Whatever has come due under the old roof is settled first, at the old rates.
_rules.rates: The new rent and Lifestyle are charged from the next month that comes due. The month already paid for is not refunded.
_rules.where: A kind of home can be rented at a building carrying every tag in allOf and none in noneOf. Which tag means which kind of home is a judgement; each row says why.
_rules.granted: A granted home is one a Role Ability hands over for nothing — the Exec's Corporate Conapt — and is offered only to a character whose Role grants it, at the same buildings creation offers.
_rules.notOffered: Living on the street (a nightly Endurance check the engine does not run yet) and the Beaverville houses an Exec is handed at Rank 7 and 10 are not on the list.

housing.why: A cube hotel is a hotel built from freight; the atlas tags exactly those.
The same buildings creation offers a starting character's container, so the home you started in is always one you could have moved to.
Ordinary housing that a company does not own and that is not a flophouse.
As a studio, less the converted containers: two bedrooms is a real flat.
Housing that cost its people, and that a company is not handing out.
As upscale, less the hotel suites: a penthouse is owned air, not a long stay.
The buildings creation offers an Exec; the luxury ones are what Rank 7 hands out, not Rank 4.
